messages:
Alex M.: Hey — I'm trying to open a PR to infra/platform-config and getting a 403 when pushing. Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config

Alex M.: I accepted the org invite but can't push. Anyone know if there's an extra team I need to be added to?

Alex M.: Error when I try to push:
```
remote: HTTP Basic: Access denied
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403
```

Taylor (IT): Quick check — did you accept with the same GitHub account you plan to use for pushes? We gate push perms by team membership (platform-ops for infra repos). Also make sure SSO provisioning finished: https://github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/people

Taylor (IT): You can also run `gh auth status` to see what account GH CLI thinks you're on.

Alex M.: Hmm I think I accepted with my personal account (alexdev). My work email is alex.m@redwood.com. How do I switch over without losing my personal account?

Jamie R.: @Alex M. you can add your work email to your existing GitHub account and verify it, then request to be added to the org team. If you'd rather keep separate accounts we can invite your work account instead, but org SSO tends to prefer a verified work email.

Jamie R.: What's your GH username? I can queue a perms request.

Alex M.: username is alexdev — I just added alex.m@redwood.com to that account and verified.

Perms Admin: Hi Alex, thanks — I saw the verification. I've added alexdev to the platform-ops team with write access to infra-config. You may need to re-auth the CLI/browser for SSO to take effect. Try `gh auth login` or sign out/in on github.com.

Alex M.: Trying a push again...

Alex M.: Success! :tada: Push went through and PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-config/pull/42

Onboarding Bot: Welcome to Redwood! If you hit more onboarding snags, ping #new-hires or @perms-admin and include your GitHub username and work email.

Alex M.: One small follow-up — is SSH preferred for pushes or is HTTPS fine? I only set HTTPS creds so far.

Taylor (IT): Either is fine but we prefer SSH for developer workflows. To add an SSH key: https://github.com/settings/keys then test with `ssh -T git@github.com`. If you want I can walk through it quickly.

Alex M.: I'll set up SSH later today. Thanks everyone for the quick help :smile:
